title: Apple Pie
description: A classic double-crust apple pie with cinnamon-spiced apple slices, a golden flaky top, and a filling allowed to set before serving.
instructions: Set the oven to 425°F and place a rimmed baking sheet on a lower rack to preheat; it will catch any juices and support browning underneath.
Roll one chilled dough disk into a round for a 9-inch pie plate. Ease it into the plate without pulling the dough, then refrigerate it while making the filling.
Combine apples, granulated sugar, brown sugar, flour, lemon juice, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt until the slices are evenly coated.
Spoon the apples into the cold crust, making a gentle mound in the centre, and scatter the diced butter across the top.
Roll out the remaining dough and lay it over the filling, or arrange it as a lattice. Trim, seal, and crimp the edge securely.
Brush with egg wash, add coarse sugar if desired, and cut vents through a solid top crust.
Bake for 20 minutes, then lower the oven to 375°F and continue for 40 to 45 minutes until the crust is richly browned and juices are bubbling through the vents.
Cool on a rack for at least 3 hours so the juices thicken enough for neat slices.
tips: Mixing tart and sweeter apples gives the filling more depth.
Cold pastry is easier to handle and bakes into a flakier crust.
Look for active bubbling in the centre before deciding the pie is done.
commonMistakes: Pulling dough to fit the plate can cause it to shrink back while baking.
Removing the pie before the filling bubbles can leave the flour undercooked and the base pale.
Cutting a hot pie releases juices before they have time to set.
substitutions: Prepared pie dough is a practical shortcut.
Allspice can replace nutmeg for a different warm spice note.
Tapioca starch may replace flour when a clearer fruit filling is preferred.
storage: Cover and keep at room temperature for up to 1 day.
Refrigerate remaining pie for up to 4 days.
Warm slices in a 325°F oven until the crust regains some crispness.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Pumpkin Pie
description: A smooth, warmly spiced pumpkin custard baked in a crisp pastry shell, made for clean slices after a proper chill.
ingredients: 3/4 cup firmly packed light or dark brown sugar
instructions: Set an oven rack in the lower third and heat the oven to 375°F. Shape the pastry in a 9-inch pie plate, finish the rim as you like, and refrigerate it while you prepare the custard.
Stir the pumpkin and brown sugar together in a large bowl until there are no pockets of sugar left in the puree.
Blend in the eggs with a whisk just until the mixture looks uniform; vigorous whisking is unnecessary and can leave extra bubbles in the baked filling.
Pour in the evaporated milk and cream, then season with cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, cloves, and salt. Whisk until the colour and spices are even throughout.
Set the cold pie shell on a sturdy rimmed tray. Add the filling, leaving the tray underneath so it is easier to transfer the full pie to the oven.

Bake until the outer portion is firm and the middle moves in one soft wave when the tray is gently shaken, about 55 to 65 minutes. If the rim darkens early, loosely cover only the pastry edge with foil.
Transfer the pie to a rack and let it come all the way to room temperature. The custard will finish settling as it cools.
Cover and chill for at least 2 hours before cutting. Add whipped cream only when ready to serve.
tips: Check the label carefully: plain pumpkin puree and sweetened pumpkin pie filling are not interchangeable.
Using a tray beneath the pie plate avoids spills and gives the soft custard stable support during transfer.
For the cleanest slices, let the pie chill fully rather than cutting it while the filling is still warm.
commonMistakes: Taking the pie out while a wide area in the centre is liquid can leave the custard too loose after chilling.
Baking until the centre is completely rigid can dry the filling and encourage cracks.
Leaving the exposed rim unprotected when it is already dark can make the pastry taste overbaked.
substitutions: Use a store-bought all-butter pie shell if preparing pastry from scratch is not practical.
Replace the individual spices with 2 teaspoons of pumpkin pie spice, then adjust to taste if the blend contains salt.
A graham cracker crust changes the texture but works well when a crumb-style base is preferred.
storage: After it has cooled, refrigerate the pie promptly and keep it covered.
Use refrigerated leftovers within 4 days.
For longer storage, wrap individual cold slices tightly and freeze for up to 1 month; thaw in the refrigerator.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Pecan Pie
description: A pecan-studded holiday pie with a buttery pastry base and a rich, set syrup filling that holds together for serving.
ingredients: 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Fit the pastry into a 9-inch pie plate, shape the edge, and keep it cold while you assemble the filling.
Scatter the pecans across the chilled shell. Reserve a few attractive halves for the surface if you would like a more defined top after baking.
In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs until blended. Stir in the corn syrup, brown sugar, melted butter, vanilla, salt, and bourbon if using until the sugar begins to dissolve.
Pour the liquid carefully over the nuts. Nudge any floating pecans into an even layer without pressing them deeply into the crust.
Put the pie plate on a rimmed baking sheet and bake for 45 to 55 minutes. It is ready when the outer filling is puffed and stable while the very centre still gives a restrained tremble.
If the pastry edge reaches a deep golden colour before the filling is done, tent just the rim with foil and return the pie to the oven.
Cool the pie on a rack for at least 3 hours before slicing so the filling can set instead of flowing at the cut edge.
Use a sharp knife for portions, wiping the blade between cuts. Serve as it is or with lightly sweetened cream.
tips: Taste a pecan before starting; fresh nuts should taste sweet and buttery rather than harsh or stale.
Place the pie plate on the baking tray before pouring in the filling, not after, to make transport safer.
A small movement in the centre is expected at the end of baking, but the filling should not look loose or sloshy.
commonMistakes: Cutting the pie before it has cooled long enough leaves the filling too soft to hold a neat slice.
Allowing the pastry edge to overbrown while waiting for the centre to finish can make the crust bitter.
Adding heavily salted pecans without reducing the added salt can unbalance the sweet filling.
substitutions: Use dark corn syrup for a deeper flavour and darker finish.
Leave out the bourbon or replace it with an equal amount of milk.
Maple syrup can replace part of the corn syrup, although the finished filling will be softer and more maple-forward.
storage: Let the pie reach room temperature before covering it.
Store leftovers in the refrigerator for up to 4 days.
Freeze tightly wrapped individual portions for up to 2 months and thaw them overnight in the refrigerator.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Key Lime Pie
description: A chilled lime custard pie with a pressed crumb base, bright citrus flavour, and a light cream finish.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Combine the graham crumbs, butter, and sugar until every crumb has a light coating of butter.
Press the mixture across the base and up the side of a 9-inch pie plate. A flat-bottomed measuring cup helps make the thickness even.
Bake the crust for about 8 minutes, until it smells toasted and looks slightly deeper in colour. Let it stand while the filling is mixed.
Whisk the yolks in a bowl, then add the sweetened condensed milk, lime juice, and zest. Continue only until the mixture is smooth and fully combined.
Pour the custard into the prepared shell and level the surface with a gentle tilt of the dish.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, stopping when the outer edge is set and the centre has only a small tremor when moved.
Cool the pie at room temperature, then refrigerate it for at least 4 hours so the filling becomes firm enough for tidy portions.
Shortly before serving, whip the cream with powdered sugar and spoon or pipe it over the cold pie. Add lime slices if desired.
tips: Use bottled Key lime juice when fresh Key limes are unavailable; choose a product made from real juice.
Press the crumb mixture firmly, especially where the base meets the side, to help the slices hold together.
Keep the pie chilled until the moment it is served for the best texture.
commonMistakes: Leaving the filling in the oven until it is entirely motionless can make the custard feel less smooth.
A lightly packed crust is likely to crumble when a slice is lifted.
Decorating with cream before the pie is cold can make the topping soften or slide.
substitutions: Regular Persian lime juice makes a good alternative, with a sharper citrus note.
Digestive biscuit crumbs can stand in for graham crumbs.
Top the finished pie with meringue instead of cream if that style is preferred.
storage: Cover and refrigerate leftover pie for up to 3 days.
Keep cream-topped portions chilled and loosely protected from absorbing refrigerator odours.
For freezing, leave off the whipped cream and freeze the wrapped pie for up to 1 month; thaw it in the refrigerator.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Cheesecake
description: A classic baked vanilla cheesecake with a compact graham base and a chilled, creamy centre.
ingredients: 24 ounces block cream cheese, at room temperature
instructions: Heat the oven to 325°F. Grease a 9-inch springform pan; if you plan to use a water bath, cover the outside with a snug layer of foil.
Mix the graham crumbs with butter and sugar until the texture is evenly sandy. Pack the mixture over the base and a short way up the pan wall.
Bake the crust for 10 minutes, then place the pan on a rack to cool while the filling is prepared.
Beat the cream cheese with sugar and salt on medium-low speed, stopping to scrape the bowl and paddle until no visible lumps remain.
Add the eggs one at a time on low speed. Mix only until each one disappears into the batter so you do not add unnecessary air.
Blend in the sour cream and vanilla, then pour the filling over the cooled crust. Smooth the surface with a spatula.
Bake for 55 to 65 minutes. The outside should appear set while the central area still moves slightly as a single mass when the pan is carefully nudged.
Let the cheesecake cool gradually, then refrigerate it for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight. Release the pan only once it is cold and slice with a warmed, wiped knife.
tips: Let the cream cheese and eggs lose their refrigerator chill before mixing for a smoother batter.
Keep the mixer on a low setting once the eggs are added to limit excess air in the filling.
The extended chill is part of the recipe: it firms the centre and makes the flavour more settled.
commonMistakes: Using cold cream cheese can leave small lumps that do not bake out.
Beating the batter hard after the eggs are added can lead to a tall rise followed by surface cracks.
Trying to portion a warm cheesecake produces untidy, soft slices.
substitutions: Vanilla wafer crumbs may be used in place of graham crumbs for a different crust flavour.
Full-fat Greek yogurt is a workable substitute for sour cream.
Add berries, caramel, or chocolate only after the cheesecake has fully chilled.
storage: Keep the cheesecake covered in the refrigerator for up to 5 days.
Freeze individual slices tightly wrapped for up to 2 months.
Thaw frozen portions in the refrigerator and serve them chilled.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: New York Cheesecake
description: Tall, dense New York cheesecake with browned edges, a creamy center, and a crisp crumb crust.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F, grease a 9-inch springform pan, and wrap the outside tightly if baking in a water bath.
Combine graham crumbs, melted butter, and sugar, press firmly into the pan, and bake the crust for 10 minutes before cooling.
Reduce the oven to 325°F and beat cream cheese until smooth before adding sugar, cornstarch, and salt in a steady stream.
Mix in sour cream, lemon juice, and vanilla on low speed, scraping the bowl so the dense filling stays smooth from top to bottom.
Add eggs and yolks one at a time, mixing only until blended after each addition to avoid adding extra air.
Pour the filling into the crust, smooth the top, and set the pan in a roasting pan with hot water halfway up the sides if using a bath.
Bake 70 to 80 minutes until the edges are puffed and lightly browned while the center still moves as one soft mass.
Turn off the oven, crack the door for 45 minutes, then cool and refrigerate overnight before slicing for the dense New York texture.
tips: Use full-fat brick cream cheese for the densest texture.
Cool slowly to reduce cracking.
Overnight chilling makes the flavor and structure better.
commonMistakes: Using whipped cream cheese changes the texture.
Skipping gradual cooling can split the surface.
Overbaking makes the center dry and crumbly.
substitutions: Use vanilla wafer crumbs for the crust.
Use a small amount of orange zest instead of lemon juice.
Serve with cherry topping on the side.
storage: Refrigerate tightly covered for up to 5 days.
Freeze whole or sliced for up to 2 months.
Thaw in the refrigerator and slice while cold.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Carrot Cake
description: Moist spiced carrot cake layered with tangy cream cheese frosting and toasted nuts.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F, grease two 9-inch cake pans, line the bottoms with parchment, and lightly flour the sides.
Whisk flour, baking soda, baking powder, cinnamon, ginger, and salt until the leaveners and spices are evenly distributed.
In a large bowl, whisk oil, both sugars, eggs, and vanilla until glossy and fully combined without needing an electric mixer.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture just until a few flour streaks remain so the cake stays tender.
Fold in grated carrots and toasted walnuts, making sure the carrots are spread evenly rather than clumped in one area.
Divide batter between pans and bake 30 to 35 minutes until the centers spring back and a tester comes out with moist crumbs.
Cool the layers in the pans for 15 minutes, then turn out and cool completely before frosting to prevent melting.
Spread cream cheese frosting between layers and over the cake, then chill briefly before slicing for clean layers.
tips: Grate carrots finely for a tender crumb.
Toast nuts before adding them.
Frost only fully cooled cake layers.
commonMistakes: Pre-shredded carrots are often too dry and coarse.
Overmixing after flour makes the cake tough.
Warm layers melt cream cheese frosting.
substitutions: Use pecans instead of walnuts.
Add raisins if desired.
Use applesauce for part of the oil for a lighter cake.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 5 days.
Bring slices near room temperature before serving.
Freeze unfrosted layers for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Red Velvet Cake
description: Soft red velvet layer cake with a light cocoa flavor and classic cream cheese frosting.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F, grease two 9-inch cake pans, line them with parchment, and dust lightly with flour.
Whisk flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt so the small amount of cocoa is evenly spread through the batter.
In a second bowl, whisk sugar, oil, eggs, buttermilk, vinegar, vanilla, and red coloring until smooth and vivid.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients in two additions, folding gently until no dry pockets remain.
Divide the batter evenly between pans and tap once or twice to release only large air pockets without deflating the batter.
Bake for 28 to 32 minutes until the centers spring back and a toothpick comes out with a few moist red crumbs.
Cool the layers fully, then level domed tops if needed and save a few crumbs for decorating the finished cake.
Fill and frost with cream cheese frosting, add reserved crumbs if desired, and chill briefly before slicing cleanly.
tips: Use buttermilk for tenderness and tang.
Measure cocoa lightly so the cake stays red.
Chill the frosted cake briefly for neater slices.
commonMistakes: Too much cocoa turns the cake brown.
Skipping vinegar weakens the classic red velvet tang.
Frosting warm layers causes sliding.
substitutions: Use gel food coloring for stronger color.
Use ermine frosting for a traditional variation.
Use sour milk if buttermilk is unavailable.
storage: Refrigerate covered for up to 5 days.
Let slices sit 20 minutes before serving.
Freeze unfrosted layers for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Brownies
description: Fudgy chocolate brownies with crackly tops, chewy edges, and rich cocoa flavor.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line an 8-inch square pan with parchment, leaving overhang so the brownies lift out cleanly.
Melt butter in a saucepan or microwave-safe bowl, then whisk in both sugars while the butter is warm to help create shiny tops.
Whisk in cocoa powder and salt until the mixture looks dark, smooth, and slightly glossy with no dry cocoa pockets.
Add eggs one at a time and whisk firmly after each addition until the batter thickens and becomes shiny.
Stir in vanilla, then fold in flour only until the last streaks disappear so the brownies stay fudgy rather than cakey.
Fold in chocolate chips, spread the thick batter evenly in the pan, and smooth the corners so the slab bakes evenly.
Bake 28 to 32 minutes until the top is crackly and a tester inserted near the center comes out with moist crumbs.
Cool completely before lifting from the pan and slicing with a sharp knife for clean squares and intact fudgy centers.
tips: Warm butter helps dissolve sugar for a shiny crust.
Use a metal pan for defined chewy edges.
Slightly underbake for fudgy centers.
commonMistakes: Overmixing flour makes brownies tough.
A clean toothpick usually means overbaked brownies.
Cutting warm brownies creates ragged edges.
substitutions: Use dark chocolate chips for deeper flavor.
Add walnuts if desired.
Use espresso powder to intensify the chocolate.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for up to 4 days.
Refrigerate for firmer fudgy texture.
Freeze squares for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Blondies
description: Chewy brown sugar blondies with buttery vanilla flavor and golden crackly tops.
ingredients: 1 cup white chocolate chips or chopped pecans
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line an 8-inch square pan with parchment, leaving enough overhang to lift out the slab.
Whisk melted butter and brown sugar until the mixture looks glossy and cohesive, which helps the bars bake chewy.
Add the egg, yolk, and vanilla, then whisk until the batter is smooth and slightly thickened from the extra yolk.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt separately so the small amount of leavener is evenly distributed before mixing.
Fold the dry ingredients into the butter mixture gently until only a few flour streaks remain in the thick batter.
Fold in white chocolate chips or pecans, spread the batter evenly into the pan, and smooth the top to the corners.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes until the edges are set, the top is lightly crackled, and the center no longer looks wet.
Cool completely in the pan before lifting out and cutting into squares so the chewy centers hold their shape.
tips: Use packed brown sugar for deep caramel flavor.
Do not overbake; the center firms as it cools.
A parchment sling makes clean removal easy.
commonMistakes: Using hot butter with eggs can scramble them.
Overbaking makes blondies dry and cakey.
Cutting before cooling causes the centers to collapse.
substitutions: Use dark chocolate chips instead of white chocolate.
Add toasted pecans for crunch.
Use browned butter for a nuttier flavor.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for up to 4 days.
Refrigerate for a firmer chewy texture.
Freeze squares for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Vanilla Cake
description: A classic American vanilla layer cake with a soft golden crumb and fluffy vanilla buttercream.
ingredients: 1 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
3 tbsp heavy cream or whole milk
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease two 9-inch round cake pans, line the bottoms with parchment paper, and lightly grease the parchment.
Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt in a medium bowl until the leavener is evenly distributed through the flour.
Beat softened butter and granulated sugar together until pale and fluffy, about 3 minutes, scraping the bowl so no dense butter pockets remain.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition, then mix in the vanilla extract until the batter smells fragrant and smooth.
Add the dry ingredients in three additions, alternating with the milk in two additions, mixing on low speed just until each addition disappears.
Scrape the bottom and sides of the bowl, then divide the batter evenly between the prepared pans and smooth the tops.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the centers spring back lightly and a toothpick inserted near the middle comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool the layers in the pans for 15 minutes, then turn them onto racks, remove the parchment, and cool completely before frosting.
For the buttercream, beat softened butter until creamy, then add powdered sugar, vanilla, cream, and salt and beat until fluffy and spreadable.
Frost one cooled layer, stack the second layer on top, cover the cake with the remaining buttercream, and let it stand briefly before slicing.
tips: Room-temperature butter, eggs, and milk make a smoother batter.
Cream butter and sugar thoroughly for a lighter crumb.
Cool layers completely before frosting.
commonMistakes: Overmixing after adding flour can make the cake tough.
Cold ingredients can cause the batter to curdle.
Underbaking leaves the center dense and fragile.
substitutions: Use cake flour for an even softer crumb.
Use buttermilk instead of whole milk for a slight tang.
Use milk instead of cream in the frosting, adding it gradually.
storage: Store covered at room temperature for up to 2 days.
Refrigerate covered slices for up to 5 days.
Freeze unfrosted layers tightly wrapped for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
